articles.title: Raphinha ya se sienta en el trono
articles.standfirst: Retabet da un vuelco a su mercado de máximo goleador de LaLiga tras el hat-trick del brasileño ante el Sevilla
articles.summary: Retabet da un vuelco a su mercado de máximo goleador de LaLiga tras el hat-trick del brasileño ante el Sevilla
articles.body: Raphinha atraviesa un momento de forma inédito en su carrera. El brasileño, convertido esta temporada en el delantero centro de referencia del Barcelona, firmó un impecable hat-trick ante el Sevilla que le permite alcanzar los doce goles en apenas seis jornadas de LaLiga, ampliando así su ventaja sobre Kylian Mbappé en la lucha por el Trofeo Pichichi. El capitán azulgrana no solo lidera en solitario la tabla de goleadores, sino que además encabeza una tabla en la que le siguen, ya a bastante distancia, jugadores como Aubameyang o Roberto Fernández. Ese rendimiento se ha trasladado de inmediato al mercado de casas de apuestas. Retabet paga ahora a cuota 1.54 que Raphinha se proclame máximo goleador de LaLiga esta temporada, situándolo como claro favorito en las apuestas deportivas por primera vez desde el arranque del campeonato. Se trata de un movimiento significativo, ya que hasta hace apenas unas semanas era Mbappé quien encabezaba con claridad este mercado tras haberse proclamado Pichichi la pasada campaña. Ahora el francés aparece como segunda opción, a cuota 1.81, una diferencia que confirma hasta qué punto la reconversión de Raphinha como ariete está dando resultado. Más alejado en las quinielas aparece Lamine Yamal, a cuota 5.8. El canterano azulgrana, que también estrenó su casillero goleador con un doblete ante el Rayo Vallecano, no suele actuar como delantero puro, lo que limita su volumen de ocasiones respecto a Raphinha o Mbappé, aunque su capacidad de desequilibrio y su instinto goleador lo mantienen como una alternativa a tener en cuenta pese a jugar habitualmente desde la banda derecha. El resto de candidatos aparece ya a una distancia considerable de los tres primeros favoritos. Ante Budimir, histórico referente goleador de Osasuna, se paga a cuota 31, mientras que Roberto Fernández, delantero revelación del Espanyol, y Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, gran capitán goleador del Deportivo en su regreso a Primera, comparten cuota a 41. Los tres han sido protagonistas puntuales en este arranque de temporada, pero el mercado no los ve todavía como amenazas reales para el dúo de cabeza. Con estos datos sobre la mesa, la pelea por el Trofeo Pichichi se perfila como uno de los grandes atractivos de la temporada. La irrupción de Raphinha en una posición que no era la suya habitual ha añadido un elemento de sorpresa a una carrera que, año tras año, suele decantarse entre los grandes referentes de Barcelona y Real Madrid. Mbappé, pese a haber cedido el liderato, cuenta con la calidad y la regularidad suficientes para reengancharse a la pelea en cualquier momento, mientras que Raphinha buscará mantener su explosión goleadora ahora que ha asumido plenamente el rol de killer en el ataque de Hansi Flick. Restan todavía más de treinta jornadas por disputarse, tiempo de sobra para que este duelo particular siga deparando capítulos apasionantes.

articles.title: Why Bryce Young Has Impressed Gronk and Jules: 'Really Fun To Watch'
articles.summary: Bryce Young and Jaxon Smith-Njigba each accounted for three touchdowns in Week 2, and Julian Edelman and Rob Gronkowski picked them as their Employees of the Week.
articles.body: Week 2 of the NFL season did not provide as many offensive fireworks as the opening week, but a pair of NFC stars stood out among the rest. Bryce Young and Jaxon Smith-Njigba each led their teams to victory by accounting for three touchdowns in Week 2. On the latest episode of FOX Sports' "Gronk & Jules," Edelman chose the Carolina Panthers quarterback and Gronkowski picked the Seattle Seahawks receiver as their Employees of the Week. Julian Edelman's Employee Of The Week QB Bryce YoungCarolina Panthers Young completed 23 of 36 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns, including two to Darren Waller, in a 34-3 win over the Atlanta Falcons. "I think Bryce Young had an unbelievable game," Edelman said. "Doesn't make too many self-inflicting mistakes. He'll take what the defense gives him. He hits the big opportunity when they give him the big opportunity. He's been really fun to watch, and he's coming into his own." The performance followed a Week 1 game in which Young threw for 361 yards in a 59-37 loss to the Chicago Bears. "They've scored a lot of points these last two weeks," Edelman said. "He's been getting better every week. For 5'10 at quarterback, it's crazy." Gronkowski pointed to Young's benching back in 2024 as the turning point. Head coach Dave Canales sat Young in favor of Andy Dalton after Carolina's 0-2 start to the 2024 season. "The benching was totally accurate," Gronkowski said. "It was necessary, and everyone thought there was no argument to the benching." Gronkowski said Dalton's play as the starter "kind of lit a spark," and he joked that Young took the fiery hair off Dalton and the heat that came with it. "Bryce Young has been the quarterback that the Carolina Panthers have wanted Bryce Young to be since that benching," Gronkowski said. "He gets better every year." Rob Gronkowski's Employee Of The Week WR Jaxon Smith-NjigbaSeattle Seahawks Smith-Njigba caught nine passes for 155 yards and a career-high three touchdowns in a 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. It was the first time in his career that he scored three touchdowns in one game. Drew Lock started at quarterback in place of Sam Darnold, who was out with a gluteus injury, and threw all three touchdown passes to Smith-Njigba, including an 82-yard catch on Seattle's first passing attempt of the game. "I'm going to go with JSN," Gronkowski said. "He had nine catches, 155 yards. He had three touchdowns, which is a career best for him. He proved once again why he was offensive player of the year and that it wasn't a mistake. The voters got it right. There's no doubt about it." Gronkowski said Seattle would not be 2-0 without Smith-Njigba, pointing to the receiver's touchdown in the Week 1 game against New England as a play that could have changed the outcome. The win over Arizona was Seattle's 12th in a row, including the postseason. Edelman focused on how Smith-Njigba gets separation from defenders. "He's just a really smooth route runner, and he outruns people," Edelman said. "This guy just outruns people, and he's smooth with it. He doesn't move his body when he cuts." Gronkowski went on to explain how defenders cannot tell when Smith-Njigba is going to break. "You think that's his out route, and then boom, he just breaks up again," Gronkowski said. "He's one of the hardest players to defend in all of football. He's just really special." Both players are in action again in Week 3. Young and the Panthers visit the Cleveland Browns. Smith-Njigba and the Seahawks play at the Washington Commanders. articles.title: Curt Cignetti Defends QB Josh Hoover As No. 5 Indiana Opens Big Ten Play
articles.summary: Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover’s statistics speak for themselves.
articles.body: Indiana quarterback Josh Hoover's statistics — and bloody image — speak for themselves. He's been efficient and tough through his first three games with the fifth-ranked and still unbeaten Hoosiers. He's completed more than 72% of his passes, thrown 10 touchdown passes and no interceptions while posting the second-best passing efficiency rating in the Football Bowl Subdivision. In his debut two weeks ago, Hoover threw four touchdown passes with only three incompletions and delivered an indelible image during the Hoosiers' 52-16 victory over North Texas: his bloodied face and chin strap, after an opponent yanked hard on his facemask. He apparently has no bigger fan than coach Curt Cignetti. On Monday the two-time Associated Press Coach of the Year defended his quarterback against those criticizing Hoover, the successor to Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza. "I think there is too much scrutiny on Josh Hoover right now — unfair scrutiny," Cignetti said near the end of his weekly news conference. "After watching the game tape, he missed one throw. The one he missed to (Charlie) Becker, we did a bad job picking up the blitz at running back and he had a guy in his face." Hoover provided his own critique during Saturday's postgame availability, saying there were some throws he wanted back in the 38-0 rout of Western Kentucky. Still, he finished the game 18 of 24 for 273 yards with two more TDs and no turnovers. Hoover believes he can still play better. "I think it goes back to what coach always preaches, right? There’s a standard we’re trying to play and that standard is perfection and to play to the best of our capabilities," Hoover said Saturday. "The goal is always to reach that and sometimes we fall short, so that’s the thing that keeps you driving forward. But we’ve done good stuff, have some things we have to clean up." Not much has changed for Indiana. The defending national champs have won their first three games by a total of 145-16 even though Hoover, who has a passer efficiency rating of 243.9, left each one early. The defense has pitched back-to-back shutouts for the first time since 1993 and has not allowed a point in nine straight quarters. And while Cignetti knows the numbers haven't come against the strongest schedule, he also knows this revamped Indiana team needed a lighter schedule before opening league play Friday night when they host Northwestern (2-0). "It's been a nice run," he said Saturday. "Of course, we get criticized because we kind of play an exhibition season before we go into Big Ten play. I can understand that. But those exhibition seasons have been real valuable for us. Last year, we played 16 games and we were 16-0 — I don't think anyone had done that since 1893, 1894 or something. We needed these games to learn about ourselves, our guys, where we are, and what we have to do to be the best we can be." Hoover, a transfer from TCU who initially committed to the Indiana program when he was in high school, has been vital in getting those pieces aligned. Becker, a holdover from last year's national championship run, has been the Hoosiers top receiver with 12 catches, 272 yards and six TDs, putting him on a pace to shatter the school's single season record for TD catches, 16 set by the late James Hardy. Most of the other key offensive players are new. Leading rusher Turbo Richard is a transfer from Boston College and a season-ending injury limited running back Lee Beebe Jr. to just three games at Indiana in 2025 after he left UAB. Indiana is also waiting for running back Khobie Martin to return from an arm injury. Receiver Nick Marsh had his best game yet with Indiana, catching seven passes for 81 yards and started displaying some of the potential the Hoosiers saw in the former Michigan State star. But Hoover's teammates seem pleased with his steady progression and the blunt-talking Cignetti has no complaints, either. "I’m glad he’s our quarterback," Cignetti said. articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez bought a €25 million plot on Dubai’s ‘Billionaire Island’ to build a custom mansion, after leasing their Madrid villa for €10,000 a month
articles.summary: International Sports News: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez expanded their property portfolio in 2024 with a €25 million land purchase on Dubai’s Jumeirah Bay Island, a .
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez expanded their property portfolio in 2024 with a €25 million land purchase on Dubai’s Jumeirah Bay Island, a luxury development often called “Billionaire Island”. The couple planned to build a private mansion on the waterfront plot as Ronaldo continued his career with Saudi Pro League club Al-Nassr. The purchase came after they had put their Madrid home in La Finca up for rent for €10,000 a month in 2023. The Dubai deal gave the family a permanent property base in the Gulf while adding another major asset to Ronaldo’s international real estate portfolio.What Was The Valuation Behind Cristiano Ronaldo And Georgina Rodríguez’s €25 Million Jumeirah Bay Land DealRonaldo and Rodríguez reportedly paid €25 million (£21 million/$27 million) for the Dubai plot in 2024. The land is on Jumeirah Bay Island, a man-made island shaped roughly like a seahorse and located off Dubai’s coast.The island is known for its small number of high-end homes and its location close to some of Dubai’s luxury hotels and facilities. It is connected to the mainland by a private bridge and is home to the Bulgari Resort and Bulgari Yacht Club.ge.globo reported in June 2024 that the couple had completed the purchase and planned to build a mansion for themselves and their five children. The report said the property was expected to be ready by the end of December that year.The purchase also made sense geographically for Ronaldo. His professional life had moved to Saudi Arabia after joining Al-Nassr, while Dubai offered a nearby base for the family and their wider business interests.The island’s appeal is not simply its location. Jumeirah Bay Island has become one of Dubai’s most exclusive residential areas, with a limited number of waterfront properties. Khaleej Times reported that the island has 124 sea-facing villas across the development, highlighting how limited the residential supply is.What Features Define The Custom Megamansion Development For Cristiano Ronaldo And Georgina RodríguezInstead of purchasing a finished house, Ronaldo and Rodríguez planned a home around their own requirements. Reports in 2024 linked the project to Palace Luxury Living, a UAE luxury property company.The biggest difference is that the Dubai home was planned as a private family residence rather than simply another investment property. Ronaldo and Rodríguez have five children, so the layout needed to work for a large family as well as their staff.Details reported about the planned property have included large living areas, private bedrooms, fitness facilities and outdoor spaces facing the water. The waterfront setting also gives the family direct access to the Dubai coastline.Rodríguez has also shown a strong interest in the design of the couple’s homes. Their previous residences have featured modern interiors, large open areas, marble surfaces and extensive outdoor spaces.That approach is easy to understand when looking at the size of the family’s other homes. Ronaldo’s properties have often been designed around football, fitness, privacy and family life rather than simply being luxury addresses.The Dubai mansion therefore fits into a pattern already seen across the couple’s property portfolio: large spaces, private facilities and enough room for family life without giving up the features expected from a high-end home.How Did Georgina Rodríguez’s Madrid Memories Show The Scale Of Cristiano Ronaldo’s La Finca HomeLong before Dubai became part of their property story, Rodríguez had already experienced what it was like to live in one of Ronaldo’s unusually large homes.The couple’s Madrid residence is located in La Finca, an exclusive residential development in Pozuelo de Alarcón. Ronaldo bought the property in 2010 for around €5 million while he was playing for Real Madrid.The home later became closely associated with Rodríguez through her Netflix series I Am Georgina. When she first moved into Ronaldo’s home, she admitted that its size made it difficult for her to find her way around.“The first time I came to Cristiano’s house, well I’d get lost,” Rodríguez revealed in her hit Netflix docuseries I Am Georgina. “I’d want to go to the kitchen to get water and I’d no idea where to go. Sometimes it would take me half an hour to get to the living room because I didn’t know the way back. Since I was a kid I had been so used to living in really small apartments”.She later said it took about six months before she knew the house properly.The Madrid property was designed by architect Joaquín Torres and has been reported as having seven bedrooms and nine bathrooms, along with indoor and outdoor pools and a gym. Ronaldo also added personal touches, including CR7-branded door handles.The scale of the property became even more notable after the couple decided they no longer needed to keep it solely as their family home.Why Did Cristiano Ronaldo And Georgina Rodríguez Lease Their Madrid Villa For €10,000 A MonthAfter Ronaldo left Real Madrid and later moved through Juventus and Manchester United before joining Al-Nassr, his time in Madrid became much more limited. In 2023, the couple put the La Finca property on the rental market for €10,000 a month.La Vanguardia reported that the house had been Ronaldo’s Madrid home during his Real Madrid years and was later offered for rent at that monthly price. The report also noted that the property was offered furnished.The decision meant the couple could keep the Madrid property instead of selling it while no longer using it as their main home.Reports described the residence as a large multi-level property with several bedrooms, bathrooms, a gym and swimming pools. Much of the furniture and decoration stayed in the house, allowing a tenant to move into the property without having to furnish it from scratch.The Dubai purchase then added a very different kind of property to their portfolio. Madrid represented Ronaldo’s long connection with Spain and his Real Madrid years. Jumeirah Bay, meanwhile, placed the family closer to his current life in the Gulf.The couple’s wider property holdings also include homes in Portugal and Spain, while Ronaldo’s business interests extend into the hotel industry through the Pestana CR7 brand.For Ronaldo and Rodríguez, the €25 million Jumeirah Bay plot was therefore more than another expensive address. articles.title: Davante Adams Dominates The Giants: 3 Takeaways From The Rams' Win
articles.summary: Davante Adams scored two touchdowns and powered the Rams offense in a win over the Giants on Monday night.
articles.body: SOFI STADIUM (Los Angeles) – The Los Angeles Rams rebounded from an embarrassing loss in Australia to start the year by cruising to a 28-6 victory over the visiting New York Giants on Monday Night Football in the team’s home opener. Dubbed the "Dream Team" to start the year because of the team’s blockbuster moves to secure defensive game changers like defensive end Myles Garrett, cornerback Trent McDuffie and the return of defensive tackle Aaron Donald, the Rams finally looked like a team that could possibly live up to that billing in front of the team’s home fans at SoFi Stadium. However, Los Angeles was buoyed by New York losing quarterback Jaxson Dart (knee) for the game in the first quarter. Ultimately, the Rams improved to 1-1 with the win, while the Giants dropped to 1-1. Here are my takeaways: 1.Davante Adams Goes Off Without Puka Nacua The Rams almost traded Adams to the Philadelphia Eagles this past offseason in a deal that would have brought wide receiver A.J. Brown to them in return. However, head coach Sean McVay decided to hold onto Adams in part because of his great chemistry with quarterback Matthew Stafford. With Brown now on the injured reserve with the New England Patriots due to a high ankle sprain, the decision has potentially proven to be a good one for the Rams. Without Puka Nacua on Monday because of a hip injury, Adams more than filled the void, totaling eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns. Adams led the league in receiving touchdowns with 14 in 2025. He's now tied for No. 4 in the NFL all-time with Marvin Harrison Sr. and Cris Carter with 29 two-touchdown games. As they leaned into last year, the Rams were effective using 13 personnel (three tight end sets). Per Next Gen Stats, Los Angeles used 13 personnel on 28 plays (54.9%) of the offensive snaps, averaging 10.4 yards per play and scoring two touchdowns with that personnel grouping. When the Rams used 13 personnel, that left Adams on the field as the lone receiver – and he thrived. Stafford finished with 327 passing yards and four touchdown passes, moving past Philip Rivers (425) on the all-time TD list with 426. Not all was great for the Rams, though. Kicker Harrison Mevis missed a 43-yard field goal wide left, as special teams remained an issue. And the Rams also had two turnovers – a Stafford interception on a ball forced into double coverage to Adams and a fumble by running back Kyren Williams that led to a 24-yard field goal for the Giants. 2.Jaxson Dart Becomes Latest Young QB To Suffer Injury New York lost its starting quarterback on the opening drive of the game when Dart was sandwiched between Los Angeles edge rusher Byron Young and Josaiah Steward, suffering a left knee injury. Dart left the field on his own, but after being evaluated by New York’s medical staff in the injury tent, he then went to the locker room for further evaluation. Dart did not return to the game and was replaced by veteran backup Jameis Winston. The absence of Dart severely limited the Giants’ offense. New York’s No. 1 receiver Malik Nabers also had to leave the game in the first half with a shoulder injury but later returned. With the team’s two top playmakers out, the Giants were held to 182 total yards of offense. Along with Dart, Chicago quarterback Caleb Williams suffered a hamstring injury at the end of his team’s 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings, and is week-to-week. And Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow again in a loss to the Dallas Cowboys and is out indefinitely. 3.Donald Shakes Off Rust In Return To Action After a two-year absence and months of anticipation, Donald finally took the field for the Rams. The Pittsburgh native received a loud ovation from fans during player introductions. Once the game got going, Donald was a contributor, making a big run stuff on running back Najee Harris to force a field goal near the goal line. He finished with three combined tackles and one quarterback pressure on 32 defensive snaps, playing 58.2% of the defensive plays for the Rams. "Aaron’s looked great," Rams head coach Sean McVay said before the game. "He’s really impacted a lot of positive things. I think our defense is feeding off his energy. He’s been a real positive for us." 3 ½. What's Next? The Rams will try to keep the positive vibes going with a trip to the Mile High City, taking on the Denver Broncos in Week 3 on Sunday night. The Broncos rebounded with a big home win over the Jacksonville Jaguars following a disappointing loss in their season opener against the Kansas City Chiefs. However, Los Angeles is still looking up at the 2-0 Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West division standings. The Giants will look to rebound at home against the 0-2 Tennessee Titans. All eyes will be on Dart this week and whether he can get back on the field.

articles.title: Dave Portnoy issues warning to Bears fans amid Caleb Williams’ ‘tweaked hammy’ injury reaction
articles.summary: Caleb Williams’ injury update could mean trouble for Chicago Bears fans, says Dave Portnoy. The Chicago Bears suffered a terrible 9-3 defeat at the hands of...
articles.body:
Caleb Williams ' injury update could mean trouble for Chicago Bears fans, says Dave Portnoy.

The Chicago Bears suffered a terrible 9-3 defeat at the hands of the Minnesota Vikings during the Week 2 clash of the two sides.

The bigger concern for the Bears was star quarterback Caleb Williams being carried off the field following what looked like a brutal injury.

However, many experts, like Dave Portnoy, have scoffed at Williams' reaction, as it turned out to be a right hamstring injury.

Dave Portnoy thinks Caleb Williams could have stayed on the field

Initially, Portnoy faced heavy criticism from fans for calling out Williams' overreaction to the injury. But with reports flooding in about Williams suffering only a hamstring injury, the tide has seemingly turned in favor of the Barstool Sports founder.

Portnoy used this opportunity to issue a warning to the Bears fanbase about how the Week 2 defeat could cause them trouble later in the season.

"I think it's fair to ask whether Caleb should have stayed in the game. I know a hockey player wouldn't have been carted off with a tweaked hammy," Portnoy wrote on X .

He added, "Bears probably win if he plays hurt. That division game could have playoff implications. Let's hope it doesn't come back to bite them."

Considering Williams is yet to be ruled out for Week 3, it's a sign that the QB hasn't suffered a major injury. So Portnoy's question makes sense.

After all, if Williams had stayed on the field, the Bears could have registered a win and achieved a 2-0 start to the season. Instead, they're now 1-1 following a terrible Week 2 defeat.

articles.title: Afghan cyclist who escaped Taliban wins Asian Games silver medal
articles.summary: Fariba Hashimi, who used to disguise herself as a man to train in Afghanistan, finishes second in women’s road race.
articles.body:
An Afghan cyclist who disguised herself as a man to pursue her sporting dreams has won an Asian Games silver medal, hoping it inspires other women in a country where Taliban authorities have sharply curtailed their freedoms.

Italy-based Fariba Hashimi powered home second in the women’s road race near Nagoya in Japan on Tuesday, calling the triumph “something special”.

“I can’t explain my feelings now,” said the 23-year-old, before reflecting on how she was attacked with stones and trained disguised as a man when she started out in the sport as a teenager, along with her sister Yulduz, who is also now a pro cyclist.

“I was born inside a country where the women who dream are getting attacked, and I’m really happy that I have fought against that,” she said.

“I hope that the next generation will come here and represent their country without any fear.”

The Taliban authorities returned to power in 2021 and have since imposed a series of rules limiting women’s access to education and public life, including sport.

“They took away our freedom, they took away everything from us,” said Hashimi, who hails from Faryab province in northern Afghanistan and left the country after the Taliban authorities took over.

“This silver medal can show a lot of resilience from Afghan women, and I’m really happy.

“I’m not alone; I know that behind me millions of women, from many countries, have the same dream and they are standing with me.”

After fleeing Afghanistan with the help of Italian former world champion Alessandra Cappellotto, Hashimi relocated to Italy, where she now lives and trains.

She and her sister competed at the Paris Olympics two years ago, and the 2028 Los Angeles Games are now looming into view.

“I never want to give up, and hopefully we can see [what can happen] again in Los Angeles,” she said.

Hashimi reserved a special thanks for the Japanese team for playing a part in her silver medal.

“I’m here without a mechanic, without any preparation. We brought one guy with us from the national federation, and he just drove the car,” she said.

“We were fixing the bike ourselves. I was the mechanic for myself. I was washing the bike myself.

“Thank you to the Japanese team. They were really, really nice to me [and] fixed my bike.”

articles.title: Who is Roshibina Devi? Wushu star who faced selection drama before assuring herself third successive Asian Games medal
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Naorem Roshibina Devi has already established herself as one of India's most consistent wushu performers at the Asian Games. On Tuesday, th.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Naorem Roshibina Devi has already established herself as one of India's most consistent wushu performers at the Asian Games. On Tuesday, the Manipuri athlete added another chapter to that record, assuring herself of a third successive continental medal at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.Roshibina defeated Macao, China's Chu Man Sin 5-0 in the women's Sanda 60kg quarterfinal at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall to storm into the semifinals. The victory guarantees her at least a bronze medal, extending a remarkable run that began with bronze at the 2018 Jakarta Asian Games and continued with silver at Hangzhou in 2023.Her latest medal comes after a selection controversy that had threatened to overshadow her return to the Asian Games squad.Who is Roshibina Devi?Born on December 30, 2000, in Kwasiphai Mayai Leikai in Manipur's Bishnupur district, Roshibina competes in the Sanda discipline of wushu, a combat sport that combines striking and throwing techniques.She first announced herself on the Asian Games stage at Jakarta 2018, where she competed in the women's 60kg Sanda category. Roshibina defeated Pakistan's Mubashra Akhtar in the quarterfinals to assure herself of a medal before losing to China's Cai Yingying in the semifinal.Five years later, at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games, Roshibina went one better. She reached the women's 60kg final and claimed silver after losing to China's Wu Xiaowei.Her performance at Hangzhou made her one of India's established names in wushu, and she was subsequently conferred the Arjuna Award for 2023.At Aichi-Nagoya, Roshibina has now assured herself of another podium finish. She first defeated Bangladesh's Shika Khatun in the pre-quarterfinals on Monday before producing a 5-0 victory over Chu Man Sin in the quarterfinals.She will fight in the semifinals on Wednesday with an opportunity to reach the gold-medal bout.A selection controversy before Aichi-NagoyaRoshibina's inclusion in the Indian Asian Games squad, however, was not without controversy.Divyanshi Choudhary was initially named in India's seven-member wushu squad released by the Sports Ministry on August 22, with a place in the women's 60kg Sanda category. She was subsequently replaced by Roshibina after the Wushu Association of India (WAI) reported an injury.The WAI said an MRI examination showed Divyanshi had suffered a partial high-grade ACL tear with large effusion and that medical advice required her to refrain from competitive activity and full training until recovery.Divyanshi initially strongly objected to the decision. In a video that surfaced on social media, the athlete, who hails from Kota and trains at NIS Patiala, alleged that she had been mentally and physically harassed and claimed that Roshibina had been involved in the harassment of her and her family."I am really fed up. I have been harassed so much mentally from June, July to now, it's September, I am being harassed, because she (Roshibina) wanted to go (to the Asian Games)," Divyanshi said in the video.She also claimed that she had defeated Roshibina in a selection trial and questioned why she had been removed from the squad despite saying that doctors had cleared her to compete with the injury.Divyanshi alleged that doctors had told her she could participate with her knee taped and questioned why her medical reports had been used to make the decision without adequately informing her.What did the Wushu Association say?The WAI rejected allegations that Divyanshi's removal was intended to accommodate Roshibina and maintained that the change was made solely on medical grounds.According to the federation, Divyanshi had sustained the injury during the 2026 SCO Wushu Sanda Championship in Hubei, China, in June. She returned to the national camp at NIS Patiala on August 10 after spending about a month at home.The federation said she complained of pain during training in August and, after her condition worsened, underwent an MRI at Manipal Hospital in Patiala on August 23.The MRI, according to the WAI, showed a partial high-grade ACL tear with large effusion. The report was subsequently reviewed by Sports Authority of India medical personnel and an orthopaedic doctor, who advised Divyanshi to refrain from competitive activity and full training until her recovery. Surgery was also advised, according to the federation's account.Divyanshi later said she understood the federation's decision, acknowledging that her health had to take priority and expressing her desire to return stronger for the 2030 Asian Games. However, she continued to allege that Roshibina had harassed her and her family. Those allegations have not been independently established.The Sports Ministry subsequently approved Roshibina's inclusion as Divyanshi's replacement through the injury-replacement process.Roshibina's Asian Games medal journeyWhatever the controversy surrounding her selection, Roshibina has allowed her performances in the arena to do the talking at Aichi-Nagoya.Her 5-0 quarterfinal victory over Chu Man Sin has assured India of its first wushu medal at the ongoing Games and secured Roshibina a place on the Asian Games podium for the third consecutive edition.Roshibina has also built an impressive record outside the Asian Games. She won gold at the 2017 Asian Junior Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games, while she also claimed gold at the 2023 Moscow Wushu Stars. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 3: India win first gold, assure medals in badminton and wushu on action-packed Tuesday
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: India's continental dominance in women's cricket remained unchallenged as the side delivered the country's first gold medal of the ongoing .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's continental dominance in women's cricket remained unchallenged as the side delivered the country's first gold medal of the ongoing Asian Games, while the men's badminton team produced a stunning performance against Japan to assure itself of a podium finish on an eventful Tuesday in Aichi-Nagoya.Harmanpreet Kaur and Co. hammered Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the women's cricket final to successfully defend their Asian Games title, taking India's medal tally to seven and finally adding the much-awaited gold to the country's haul.India also assured themselves medals in men's badminton and wushu, while the men's hockey side continued its goal-scoring spree with another emphatic victory, crushing Sri Lanka 16-1 in a Pool A encounter.There were contrasting fortunes in shooting and table tennis, while India's boxers continued their unbeaten run and gymnast Pranati Nayak qualified for the vault final.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medals TallyWomen's cricket deliver India's first goldIndia's women's cricket side produced another commanding performance to retain the Asian Games title.After opting to bat, India posted a mammoth 216/3, their highest-ever total in women's cricket at the Asian Games. Smriti Mandhana led the charge with a 45-ball 79, while Richa Ghosh provided a late flourish with an unbeaten 49 off just 22 balls.Shafali Verma contributed 48 from 29 balls as India dominated the gold-medal clash from the outset. The bowlers then completed the job, dismissing Sri Lanka for just 69 to seal a 147-run victory.The triumph gave India their first gold of the Aichi-Nagoya Games and their second successive women's cricket gold at the Asian Games.ALSO READ: Who is Roshibina Devi? Wushu star who faced selection drama before assuring herself third successive medalMen's badminton assure medal after stunning Japan winThe men's badminton team, silver medallists at the previous edition, produced a memorable 3-0 victory over Japan to storm into the semifinals and assure themselves of at least a bronze medal.Lakshya Sen provided the breakthrough after recovering from a difficult start against world No. 7 Kodai Naraoka. The Indian shuttler lost the opening game and was trailing 14-19 in the decider before producing a remarkable comeback to win 11-21, 21-5, 21-19.Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty then defeated former world champions Takuro Hoki and Yugo Kobayashi 21-18, 24-22 to put India 2-0 ahead.Ayush Shetty completed the job with a composed 21-10, 21-19 victory over world No. 16 Koki Watanabe, sealing India's place in the semifinals.The result also helped the men's side make up for the disappointment of the women's team's quarterfinal exit earlier in the day.Women's badminton bow outIndia's women's badminton team suffered a 1-3 defeat against Japan in the quarterfinals.Two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu gave India a strong start before eventually losing 23-21, 18-21, 6-21 to world No. 3 Akane Yamaguchi.Unnati Hooda then went down 16-21, 18-21 against 2022 world junior champion Tomoka Miyazaki.Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand kept India alive with a 21-17, 21-16 win over Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto. However, Tanvi Sharma could not force a decider, losing 12-21, 10-21 to former world champion Nozomi Okuhara as Japan sealed the tie.Roshibina assures another wushu medalRoshibina Devi Naorem continued her remarkable Asian Games run by assuring herself of a third successive medal.The Manipuri wushu player defeated Macao, China's Chu Man Sin in the women's Sanda 60kg quarterfinal at the Aichi Prefectural Martial Arts Hall. The victory took Roshibina into the semifinals and guaranteed her at least a bronze.Roshibina won bronze at the 2018 Jakarta Games and followed it with a silver at Hangzhou in 2023.Her latest medal comes after a selection controversy surrounding India's squad, with Roshibina eventually replacing Divyanshi Choudhary after the federation cited an injury.Hockey side continues goal festThe men's hockey side continued its dominant start to the competition with another massive victory, beating Sri Lanka 16-1 in its second Pool A match.Jugraj Singh scored four goals, while Abhishek Singh and Dilpreet Singh completed hat-tricks. Harmanpreet Singh also scored twice as India kept the pressure on throughout the contest.The defending champions had earlier opened their campaign with a 13-1 win over Indonesia. The two victories have given India a staggering +27 goal difference.Boxers maintain unbeaten runIndia's boxers also enjoyed a productive day.Sakshi Chaudhary pulled off one of the day's notable upsets by defeating Paris Olympic bronze medallist Aira Villegas in the women's 51kg category to enter the pre-quarterfinals.Jadumani Singh also advanced to the last 16 in the men's 55kg category, defeating Nepal's Chandra Bahadur Thapa 5-0.Pranati Nayak reaches vault finalGymnast Pranati Nayak qualified for the women's individual vault final after finishing seventh among 19 competitors in the qualification round.The three-time Asian Gymnastics Championships bronze medallist recorded a combined score of 12.916 to make the eight-gymnast final, scheduled for September 24.Mixed fortunes in table tennisIndia's women's table tennis team advanced to the quarterfinals after edging Thailand 3-2.The men's side, however, suffered a 0-3 defeat against South Korea in the round of 16 and exited the competition. The loss followed their defeat to Iran in the group stage.Shooting misses out on another medalIt was a rare disappointing day for India's shooters.Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Mane finished fourth in the 10m air rifle mixed team final after qualifying second. The pair, who had already won medals in other events, could not reproduce their qualification-round form and were eliminated with a score of 376.3.There was some encouragement in skeet, however, as Anantjeet Singh Naruka moved into a four-way tie for the lead after four rounds of qualification. The 28-year-old shot 96 out of 100 on Tuesday and now has one more round of 25 targets remaining before the eight-shooter final.More mixed results across disciplinesIndia's campaign also produced mixed results elsewhere.In fencing, Chetan Bhatt lost his bronze-medal bout in the 84kg category. The swimmers endured another difficult outing, with the men's 4x100m relay team finishing eighth and last in the final.Despite those setbacks, Tuesday proved to be another significant day for India at Aichi-Nagoya. The women's cricket title delivered the country's first gold, while medals were assured in men's badminton and wushu. With the hockey side continuing to dominate and boxers making progress, India ended the day with momentum across several disciplines.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: NEW DELHI: India finally opened its gold-medal account at the Asian Games 2026 on Tuesday as Harmanpreet Kaur-led side successfully defended its women's cricket title, beating Sri Lanka in the final at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin.The emphatic victory took India's medal tally to seven — one gold, four silver and two bronze — and moved the country to eighth place in the medal standings at the end of Tuesday's action.India's first gold in Aichi-Nagoya came after the defending champions produced a dominant all-round performance. After opting to bat, India posted a mammoth 216/3 before bowling Sri Lanka out for just 69 to complete a commanding 147-run victory.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medals TallyThe result also marked India's second women's cricket gold at the Asian Games. India had won the title when the sport returned to the Games in Hangzhou in 2023, while the country did not participate when cricket featured at the 2010 and 2014 editions.Pakistan, meanwhile, also have two women's cricket gold medals, having won the inaugural women's events in 2010 and 2014.India finally adds gold to seven-medal haulIndia had begun its Asian Games campaign with two shooting silver medals before adding three more shooting medals and a historic MMA bronze on Day 2.The women's cricket gold now gives the Indian contingent a medal distribution of one gold, four silver and two bronze. The medal tally is expected to grow further, with India having assured itself of medals in men's badminton and wushu.The men's badminton team booked a semifinal place with a 3-0 victory over Japan, while Roshibina Devi reached the women's Sanda 60kg semifinals to guarantee at least a bronze.India's men's hockey side also strengthened its campaign with a stunning 16-1 victory over Sri Lanka, adding to its 13-1 win over Indonesia in the opening Pool A match.The men's cricket competition will begin later in the Games. The Shreyas Iyer-led Indian side is scheduled to enter the competition directly in the second quarterfinal on September 28. India are also the defending men's Asian Games champions.China continue to lead, Japan secondChina continued to occupy the top position in the medal standings, with Japan in second and South Korea third.China's dominance has been particularly visible in swimming, where 13-year-old Yu Zidi has emerged as one of the stars of the Games. Hosts Japan also celebrated a teenage swimming sensation, with 17-year-old Yumeki Kojima winning the men's 400m individual medley in a Games-record 4:07.02.China also added more gold through its shooters, with Olympic champion Sheng Lihao combining with Wang Zifei to win the 10m air rifle mixed team event with a world-record score of 507.1.Afghanistan also celebrated a historic medal after Fariba Hashimi won silver in the women's road race, becoming the country's first female Asian Games medallist in cycling.Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally after Day 3RankCountryGoldSilverBronzeTotal1China32138532Japan111619463South Korea6417274Kazakhstan615125Thailand41166Hong Kong, China354127Tajikistan21148INDIA14279Uzbekistan141610Chinese Taipei1359Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026: Unease in India rowing camp as last-minute crew changes leave athletes ‘disturbed’
articles.summary: Asian Games 2026 News: NEW DELHI: Uneasiness is brewing in India's rowing camp ahead of the start of the Asian Games competition on Wednesday, with several rowers expressing.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uneasiness is brewing in India's rowing camp ahead of the start of the Asian Games competition on Wednesday, with several rowers expressing unhappiness over last-minute changes to crew combinations and event entries.Some athletes have alleged that they were shifted from their original events while reserve rowers were brought into first-team combinations following a meeting of team managers on Monday. The developments have left some members of the squad "very disturbed", according to a rower who spoke to PTI on condition of anonymity."Some rowers have not taken food yet as they are in a disturbed state of mind. They are not knowing what to do," the rower told PTI on Monday.An official tracking the developments within the rowing team also confirmed that some athletes were struggling to deal with the changes."It is very sad, but things are not rosy in the rowing team," the official said.Asian Games Full Coverage | Schedule | Medal TallyRowers upset over last-minute changesAs per reports, the 2022 Asian Games silver medallist Arvind Singh, who was originally scheduled to compete in the single sculls, has been moved to the quadruple sculls. Balraj Panwar, who was part of the quadruple sculls combination, is set to compete in the single sculls instead.Saurav Kumar and Vipul Satish, who were to form the first-choice men's pair, are set to be replaced by Nitin Kumar and Jaswinder Singh. Reserve rower Jasmail Singh is also set to be included in the coxless four.Navdeep Singh and Kulwinder Singh are expected to move from the double sculls to the quadruple sculls.A senior rowing official said 50 per cent of a crew can be changed in case of a medical emergency, while athletes have questioned the scale of the changes made this time.The rowers' frustration was still evident on Tuesday, although they eventually returned to practice ahead of the competition.“We are going by what our manager has told us. We will be giving our best when we enter the water, but they shouldn’t have done this,” one of the rowers told TOI on condition of anonymity.“It has brought a lot of pressure and anxiety. I couldn’t sleep last night, I was very disturbed. A crew combination is set for six months or one year. We have been practising for long, and when it is changed one day before such a big competition, the athlete gets disturbed mentally. Crew combination is important in rowing. Someone who is not in quad (quadruple) for six months, what is he going to achieve in one day?”Management cites shortened programmeThe rowing management, however, has defended the changes, saying they were necessitated by the shortened competition schedule after heavy rains.Antony Patterson, India's Australian head coach, said the priority was to maximise India's medal opportunities rather than preserve individual event combinations.“Due to the shortened regatta programme, I as the chief coach has made the decision to focus on possible medals, not individual comfort of athletes,” Patterson said on Monday.Rowing Federation of India president Balaji Maradapa also said the revised schedule made it difficult for athletes to compete in multiple events as originally planned.“Originally it was four plus one day of races. Now it is just two days and four sessions of races each day. How can you be doubling,” Balaji said.The competition, originally scheduled to begin on Monday, will now be held on Wednesday and Thursday. Balaji said all participating teams had been allowed to change their entries following the revision in schedule.‘We will do it for the country’Despite their frustration, the rowers have vowed to put the controversy aside once competition begins at the Nagaragawa regatta course.“But it’s okay, whatever that has happened is God’s will. Whatever event we enter, we won’t give up until we die. Which ever athlete it is, he will give his life because this chance, this platform, is not something one gets everyday, but once in four years.“But what happened was wrong,” the rower said.He also said the athletes were informed about the changes rather than consulted, adding that their position within the Army made it difficult to openly challenge the decision.“We are under the Army. We compete as a team. If there is any indiscipline, we will never be able to row again,” he said.The rower, however, insisted that the squad would give everything once on the water.“Ye Hindustan ki baat hai, Tirange ki baat hai. We have come here to achieve something big, and we will,” he said. “We will do it for the country. We won’t return home without a medal.”India's rowing campaign begins on Wednesday, with the team hoping to put the last-minute turmoil behind it and translate its preparations into medals.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire Pickups, Week 3: Jonah Coleman, Tre Tucker among top targets to add
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his fantasy football waiver wire column for Week 3.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

If you've been reading this column, you're going to recognize a lot of the names featured this week. Young was my top QB add heading into Week 2, after an outstanding fantasy performance in the opener and he followed it up with another three-touchdown effort on Sunday.

The 25-year-old former first overall pick is the second-highest scoring fantasy quarterback through two games, behind only Josh Allen.

Jalen Coker has formed a strong receiver tandem with Tetairoa McMillan and Darren Waller is emerging as a dangerous red-zone weapon for the Panthers. The veteran tight end scored two touchdowns against the Falcons and had another called back on a penalty in Week 1.

There's no reason to think this party will stop anytime soon, with the Browns and Lions next up on the schedule for Carolina. Consider Young a borderline low-end QB1 for those matchups.

Kyler Murray is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 QB add, if available.

Risky streaming options (if starter is out)

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

Encouraging people to draft Coleman in the late rounds was my mission throughout the summer and I reserved room to write about him in each of the first two waiver wire columns this season.

Stashing Coleman was speculative, since he was technically the Broncos' No. 3 back behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. However, given Dobbins' injury history (missed time in all six of his NFL campaigns) it seemed almost inevitable that a path would be cleared at some point this season. The coaching staff and beat writers also strongly suggested that Coleman was the direct Dobbins' replacement, not Harvey.

Even with all that in mind, I certainly didn't expect to see Coleman's opportunity arrive in Week 2. With Harvey sidelined due to a hamstring injury, the rookie had a chance to see the field more on Sunday. Then, Dobbins suffered a hamstring injury of his own, which paved the way for Coleman to help lead the Broncos to victory with 58 scrimmage yards and a score on 13 touches.

While we wait for updates on both injury statuses, this is your last chance to pick up Coleman … and you're going to have to spend a significant amount of your budget to do it. Don't worry, he'll be worth it. Dobbins hasn't looked particularly good this season prior to getting hurt and Sean Payton raved about Coleman throughout the preseason. He might just take this job and not give it back, with Harvey eventually returning to his pass-catcher-plus role, when healthy.

Bigsby has been one of the better one-injury away backups to have on your bench, but that became even more important on Sunday when Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger and missed a large portion of the game. Bigsby took advantage, posting 38 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Titans.

Though Barkley is headed for an early-week MRI, the initial reports seem optimistic that this won't be a serious issue.

Regardless, Bigsby needs to be rostered. If Barkley were to miss a game, Bigsby would step in as the Eagles' lead back and a potential fantasy RB2, with Will Shipley operating as a pass-catching option.

Wilson is also seeing value inflated due to a starter getting banged up. Rookie Jadarian Price is dealing with a shoulder injury that caused him to miss time in the late stages of Sunday's game.

Just like Barkley, Price is going to get evaluated over the next couple days, but the early reports suggest this isn't anything major.

With Price missing time, Wilson leapfrogged George Holani and took over as the early-down back for the Seahawks. The result was a solid 92 yards on 21 carries.

If Price is unable to suit up for Week 3, Wilson would be a borderline low-end RB2 for fantasy in a matchup where Seattle is 6.5-point favorites over the Commanders. Keep in mind, Zach Charbonnet is expected to return in October, so the runway is short for Wilson.

Kaelon Black is 56% rostered but would be the No. 4 RB add behind Coleman, Bigsby and Wilson, if available.

Tyler Allegeier is 51% rostered but would be the No. 5 RB add behind Coleman, Bigsby, Wilson and Black, if available.

Zach Charbonnet is 51% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

The more things change, the more they look the same — and the top of the receiver section is identical to last week.

Perhaps it was concerns about the Browns' quarterback situation that kept managers from being more aggressive in adding Boston, but all the signs were there.

The second-rounder led Browns wideouts in snaps by a wide margin in Week 1, running a route on 97% of their dropbacks. He caught four passes for 59 yards and a 46-yard touchdown in his debut.

In Week 2, he picked up where he left off with a 94% route share and an even bigger stat line of 5-95-1 on seven targets.

As I said last week, we have a long way to go before having faith in a Deshaun Watson-led passing game, but fantasy managers need to pay attention to what Boston is doing. He's an absolute must-add and a potential fantasy WR3/flex with upside moving forward.

I'm hesitant to invest in a big Tucker game because we've seen this before with the speedy wideout. During his career, Tucker has popped up for a sizable stat line once or twice per season, before falling back to earth in the rest of his games.

Keep that in mind if you're planning to chase Tucker's five-catch, 119-yard, one-touchdown result from Week 2.

With Brock Bowers likely to return next week, Tucker's volume will be even more sporadic. He still has value as a splash-week WR4/flex option, just don't let your expectations run wild thinking this will be a weekly occurrence.

Bateman filled the void left by the absences of Zay Flowers (hamstring) and Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist), putting up seven catches, 88 yards and a touchdown versus the Saints.

Much like Tucker, I don't expect this to become the new norm for Bateman, but we might see another strong fantasy start out of him in Week 3 if Flowers remains on the sidelines.

With the Ravens traveling to Brazil to take on the Cowboys and concerns about the quality of the field already making headlines, Baltimore would be foolish to risk re-injury to their star wideout. If Flowers sits, Bateman will be a WR3/flex option with a much higher ceiling for one more week.

Devaughn Vele is 51% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Boston, if available.

Jordyn Tyson is 53% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Gadsden starting the season buried on the depth chart behind David Njoku and Charlie Kolar was a strange development after the flashes we witnessed from him as a rookie.

However, the fantasy landscape is always evolving and Gadsden is on the verge of getting another significant opportunity after Njoku (knee) was carted off and Kolar (forearm) was seen in a sling.

Meanwhile, Gadsden found the end zone versus the Raiders, which brought back memories of his breakout month in 2025, when he posted 7-68-0, 7-164-1, 5-77-1, and 5-68-0 from Week 6 to Week 9.

While I doubt he reaches that level of production, Gadsden is back in the conversation as a TE2 streamer with TE1 upside in a Chargers offense that could use a spark.

Dalton Schultz is 56% rostered but would be the No. 1 TE add, if available.

Hunter Henry is 56% rostered but would be the No. 2 TE add behind Schultz, if available.

Favorable upcoming schedules: Chiefs (34% rostered), Bills (14% rostered), Saints (1% rostered)

Here are some players you can consider cutting from your roster to free up room on your bench for this week's top waiver wire adds.

Quarterbacks: Baker Mayfield, Malik Willis

Running Backs: Rico Dowdle, Kenny Gainwell, Chris Rodriguez Jr.

Wide Receivers: Marvin Harrison Jr., Courtland Sutton, Jayden Reed

Tight Ends: Brenton Strange, Michael Mayer

Mayfield was unable to top 13 points in either of the first two games against the Bengals and Browns. Now, he'll have to take on Brian Flores' Vikings defense. Better days will come eventually, but he's just a bye-week replacement QB2.

The idea that Gainwell would be a weekly flex option, while also offering one-injury away upside has not materialized. He's managed just 33 scrimmage yards on 11 touches through the first two games. If he's still on your roster, it's just as a stash in case Bucky Irving gets hurt at some point.

Rodriguez is a limited player with no role in the passing game. Similar to Gainwell, he has just 36 yards on 12 carries. Even if Bhayshul Tuten were sidelined, Rodriguez would max out as a TD-or-bust RB3 for fantasy.

It's not happening for Harrison in Arizona. After hauling in just one catch for 33 yards on three targets in the opener, he failed to record a reception in Week 2 with only one pass thrown in his direction. The only chance for fantasy redemption might be in a fresh start with a new organization.

articles.title: Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup: Wales pick two fathers and sons for Australia
articles.summary: Fathers and sons Martin and Matthew Turner and Gareth Ramsey and Sid Ramsey are named in Wales' squad for the 2026 Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup.
articles.body:
Wales have named two pairs of fathers and sons - Martin and Matthew Turner and Gareth and Sid Ramsey - in their squad for the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup in Australia.

It is the first time a father and son have represented Wales together at a Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup and the first time two such pairings have been named in one squad.

A father-and-son pair have featured in the Wales set-up previously, but never before on the World Cup stage.

Head coach Alan Caron included them in his 12-strong selection for the tournament, which starts for Wales against England on Friday, 30 October in Wollongong.

Group games against Ireland and the United States follow at the same venue as the teams aim for the knockout stages.

Gareth Ramsey, John Berriman and Fionn McCabe - who turns 16 shortly before the competition - could make Wales debuts during the event.

Caron said: "Having two father-and-son combinations in the squad makes this World Cup particularly special.

"Gareth and Sid, and Martin and Matthew, have the opportunity to share something that very few players ever get to experience: representing Wales together at a World Cup.

"For John, Fionn and Gareth, the opportunity to make their Wales debuts at a World Cup would be something very special, while our experienced players will be vital in helping them and the rest of the squad through the tournament."

Wales have had to fundraise to help with the costs of taking the squad to Australia, with more than half of the £10,000 target donated so far.

Stuart Williams (Edinburgh Giants/North Wales Crusaders), Jodie Boyd-Ward (Leeds Rhinos), Andrew Higgins (Midlands Hurricanes), Lee Sargent (Midlands Hurricanes/Cardiff Blue Dragons), Jonathan Gill, Fionn McCabe, Martin Turner (all North Wales Crusaders), Gareth Ramsey, Sid Ramsey (both Sheffield Eagles), Matthew Turner (Wigan Warriors/North Wales Crusaders), Mark Williams (Wigan Warriors/South Wales Jets), John Berriman (York RLFC).

articles.title: Wisconsin volleyball may be 'little bit closer' to consistent starting lineup
articles.summary: As Wisconsin volleyball begins Big Ten play, Kelly Sheffield suggested the Badgers may be a 'little bit closer' to a consistent starting lineup.
articles.body:
MADISON – Wisconsin volleyball coach Kelly Sheffield has been happily employed at UW for 13-plus years, but his playing time analogy might be more fitting for someone who is not quite as fortunate.

"When you've had a job interview and you don't hear from somebody for a while, you get to the point of, 'Just tell me no,'" Sheffield said. "'No' is actually better than not knowing. Or maybe it's the same thing if you've asked somebody out on a date that you haven't heard back from. … Playing time might be a little bit like that."

The Badgers have been living in that uncertainty for the first several weeks of the season, as Sheffield has gone with 10 different starting lineups in UW's first 10 matches.

"It's not that I don't have urgency and that we're not trying to win," Sheffield said. "But when you got 11 new people, I wasn't interested in making decisions on just about two weeks of information."

Wisconsin women's volleyball vs. Florida at the UW Field House

Twelve UW players have appeared in at least 15 of the team's 38 sets played in the nonconference schedule, and that does not count 2025 third-team All-American Jaela Auguste or highly touted freshman Decelise Champion .

"That's really unusual for me or probably about anybody at this point, especially when you're in a sport that you have a limited number of subs," Sheffield said.

Wisconsin 's fluidity in the lineup – while helpful for Sheffield to learn more in August and September before more consequential matches in November and December – has its drawbacks as well.

"For others, that can be stressful," Sheffield said. "And knowing what the tendency of the person is next to you – are they a little bit stronger in this seam? Or they pull back a little bit?"

Sheffield now thinks the Badgers are a "little bit closer to getting locked in" with a consistent starting lineup.

While UW is not entirely at full strength – Grace Egan's timeline to return remains murky as she recovers from a back injury – the Badgers are closer than they have been all season.

Auguste returned in the Badgers' loss to then-No. 9 Texas and started in the next two matches after missing five matches. Champion, meanwhile, has acclimated to UW, appeared in the last four matches and started in the last two matches.

Along with Auguste and Champion's availability, past starting lineups have offered some hints about what the starting lineup might look like on a consistent basis.

Setter Charlie Fuerbringer and outside hitter Audrey Flanagan have started in all 10 matches. Anna Bardaro has been the starting libero in eight matches and a starting defensive specialist in one of the other matches. Middle blocker Lynney Tarnow has started the last nine matches.

As Big Ten play begins with a Sept. 24 home match against No. 20 Oregon and a Sept. 27 trip to No. 10 Purdue, a consistent lineup is just one of the things on Sheffield's to-do list with a team that has more newcomers than returners.

"I would say it's a long list," Sheffield said. "It's not just one or two. But honestly, show me a coach that doesn't have a laundry list of things that they want or a conveyor belt of things that they want to get better at. It's part of the joy."

articles.title: Sebastien Bourdais joins DragonSpeed Corvette lineup in GTD Pro return at Petit Le Mans
articles.summary: Two-time overall Petit Le Mans winner headlines a stacked Corvette entry in his first GT start since 2019
articles.body:
DragonSpeed is set to make a return to the GTD Pro class of the IMSA WeatherTech SportsCar Championship for its final scheduled series appearance of the season at next weekend's Motul Petit Le Mans, signing Sebastien Bourdais to headline the effort.

The Cadillac factory driver, who will depart Hertz Team JOTA's FIA World Endurance Championship program at the end of the season, will team up with DragonSpeed regulars Giacomo Altoe and Casper Stevenson behind the wheel of the Chevrolet Corvette Z06 GT3.R.

Bourdais brings significant momentum to Michelin Raceway Road Atlanta, having twice won the grueling 10-hour Endurance Cup round overall. The upcoming race marks his first GT start since the conclusion of the Chip Ganassi Racing-run Ford GT program in 2019.

The announcement came via DragonSpeed's social media channels.

"Getting a call up from DragonSpeed and being asked to race with them really put a smile on my face," Bourdais said.

"I love Petit, and have been fortunate to have a lot of success there in the past. This will be my third different class in the last three years and I'm really excited to see how different it is to what I've experienced for the previous two times.

"Racing in GTD Pro in a Corvette will also be two new ventures, but everyone I've talked to says the Chevy is a great car.

"The focus of the weekend is to help DragonSpeed, Elton, Henrik, Giacomo, Casper and all the guys behind the scenes get a win at Petit for GM!"

The event will mark the Elton Julian-led squad's first appearance back in GTD Pro since finishing runner-up in the class championship last year, following a strong campaign with a privateer Ferrari 296 GT3 program that took the fight to factory-backed efforts.

"Ah, Petit Le Mans… One of my favorites. So ready to finish this year with a classic both in and out of the car," said Julian.

"Over the years, DragonSpeed has raced with some of the great drivers of their generation, whether it be in endurance or single-seaters. Sebastien is one of those drivers.

"When the decision was taken to race in Pro to close out our GT campaign in IMSA, we needed an ace in the pocket and we found one. With him, I know what we are going to get and it's exactly what we will need.

"It's time to go racing again with the big boys and we won't bring a knife to a gun fight. Everyone at DragonSpeed and GM are looking forward to seeing him do his thing in the Z06 GT3.R."

articles.title: Nick Sirianni Gave Detailed Game Plan for Zach Ertz After Eagles Signing
articles.summary: Everyone in Philly is still celebrating after the news that the Philadelphia Eagles have signed team legend Zach Ertz.The Eagles are bringing in Ertz to add...
articles.body:
Everyone in Philly is still celebrating after the news that the Philadelphia Eagles have signed team legend Zach Ertz .

The Eagles are bringing in Ertz to add depth at tight end. Dallas Goedert will miss a few weeks with a sprained MCL injury he suffered in the Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans .

There's been plenty of reaction, but Eagles fans want to hear from head coach Nick Sirianni. The head coach has revealed the plan for Ertz.

Nick Sirianni Shares Philadelphia Eagles' Plan for Zach Ertz

Sirianni made his weekly appearance on SportsRadio 94 WIP in Philadelphia, where he spoke about the Ertz signing for the first time. He said he had actually stayed connected with him.

"Obviously, we talk about everything, and every decision's so well thought out. Just excitement to bring Zach back. Zach, I obviously got to spend time with him early in my time here, not the entire season, but really like the person. Obviously, the player is legendary for everything that he's done and I always thought he was a good teammate, good person, and I've kept in touch with him and we've obviously played him multiple times since he's left here. So being able to chat with him before and after games is always fun. Excited to have him back."

A follow-up question was about how soon Ertz can make an impact on this offense. Sirianni made sure to tame expectations with the fan base.

"We'll see. You know, that's, that's hard to, that's hard to predict. We got to get him out there. We got to get practice. Practice is obviously so important to our weekly process for us to feel good about plays that we're going to be running in the game, or defenses that we're going to be running in the game, or situations to practice, and also players. We'll get through this week and see where he is. Everyone knows he's coming off of an injury, but the guy has always been a great worker. Just wants to be great. I can only imagine that he's in a great spot right now, and we'll see where it is once we get a little later in the week."

Ertz has played in 123 career games with the Eagles from 2013 through 2021. He caught 579 passes for 6,267 yards and 38 touchdowns .

When Will Zach Ertz Help the Eagles in 2026?

Ertz is a weapon that the Eagles can't keep on the sidelines, so he should play right away. The question will be how soon he can make an impact on this offense.

He needs a realistic timeline since he has to get into shape and learn the offense. He should still play in Week 3 against the Chicago Bears . Even better, he has an extra day since they play Monday night.

Jalen Hurts and Ertz might need some time to work out together and get the chemistry back on track. That said, the Eagles need a solid receiving tight end right away, with Goedert and Eli Stowers hurt. They only have Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins right now, so Ertz arrives in Philly at the perfect time to make an immediate impact.

articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams bounced back with a convincing Week 2 victory, but the status of star wide receiver Puka Nacua remains unclear ahead of their matchup a...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams bounced back with a convincing Week 2 victory, but the status of star wide receiver Puka Nacua remains unclear ahead of their matchup against the Denver Broncos .

Nacua was a late scratch from the Rams' 28-6 victory over the New York Giants on Monday Night Football because of a hip/groin injury. Los Angeles improved to 1-1 in a game that also marked Aaron Donald's return , but head coach Sean McVay offered little clarity Tuesday regarding whether Nacua will be available in Week 3.

Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times shared McVay's update on X, formerly known as Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I'm not sure what his status is as far as this next coming week. I'm hopeful that he'll play," McVay said. "If he's ready to go, great. If not, then we'll continue to roll."

ESPN's Sarah Barshop also reported that McVay remains uncertain about Nacua's availability against Denver.

"I'm hopeful that he'll play," McVay said, according to Barshop.

Puka Nacua 's status remains uncertain for Rams-Broncos matchup

Nacua's late absence against New York forced the Rams to adjust their receiving rotation shortly before kickoff. While Los Angeles still produced 28 points and secured its first victory of the season, Nacua's availability remains an important storyline as the team prepares for its first road game since returning from its season-opening matchup in Australia.

The Rams opened the season with a 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers before responding with a 22-point victory over the Giants.

McVay's comments indicate Los Angeles is hopeful Nacua can return against Denver, but the team does not appear prepared to push the receiver onto the field if the hip/groin issue continues to bother him.

His practice participation throughout the week should provide additional information about his chances of playing.

The Rams will now turn their attention to the Broncos , who also enter Week 3 with a 1-1 record. Los Angeles and Denver are scheduled to meet Sunday at 5:20 p.m. PT on NBC.

articles.title: Why .991 OPS prospect is reason Rangers can be optimistic for 2027 MLB season
articles.summary: This top Rangers' prospect is why there's hope for the 2027 season and beyond.
articles.body:
The 2026 season for the Texas Rangers has been far from ideal. But at 78-78 entering the final week of play before the postseason begins, the Rangers are in the lead for the AL West title.

They might back into the division title and a home-field playoff series, most likely against the Chicago White Sox , during the Wild Card round. But if looking beyond the strange 2026 season for the Rangers, why should fans have optimism for 2027 and beyond?

Levi Weaver of The Athletic revealed the reason why: their .991 OPS top prospect, Sebastian Walcott, should give Rangers fans a lot of hope for the future, starting in 2027.

Sebastian Walcott should give Rangers fans hope in 2027 and beyond

"One reason to believe in next year: Well ... there is this one really good prospect?" Weaver writes. "... So as I look forward to 2027, the biggest optimism magnet is easily prospect Sebastian Walcott."

Walcott is a 20-year-old top prospect for the Rangers who can slot into third base or shortstop. Finding a spot for him on the MLB roster might be a bit tricky, but the Rangers should try their best to get him up in 2027.

In 41 games this year, after missing most of the season due to a UCL injury he has been recovering from, Walcott has a .325 batting average with a .991 OPS.

Across 166 at-bats, Walcott has 48 runs scored, 54 hits, 14 doubles, 10 home runs, 21 RBIs, 19 walks, and 13 stolen bases. It's been arguably the best stretch of his professional career.

There are plenty of issues with the 2026 Rangers roster, but looking into the future, Walcott is someone that the Rangers and their fans can get very excited about.

As Weaver put it, Walcott is an "optimism magnet" for the Rangers as they close out what's been a very underwhelming and frustrating 2026 season.

But so long as Walcott is healthy and the Rangers call him up to the big leagues next year, there's some real reason for optimism for this Rangers team in 2027 and beyond.

There are plenty of other players, like Wyatt Langford and Corey Seager , whom Rangers fans should be excited about next year. But Walcott's potential promotion should be what Rangers fans most look forward to next season.

articles.title: David Stone injury update: OU football DL's initial X-rays on knee 'positive'
articles.summary: OU football star defensive lineman David Stone was injured in practice Monday. Here's the latest update from Sooners coach Brent Venables.
articles.body:
NORMAN — Oklahoma defensive lineman David Stone was injured during Monday's practice while going up against the scout team's offense, coach Brent Venables said Tuesday.

Despite a report that circulated Monday night, Venables said Stone's injury did not occur while the defensive lineman was on offense. The Sooners ' coach said initial X-rays were positive but that his status for this week's game against Georgia is unclear.

"If David is unavailable this week, we're going to need some guys to step up and play big," Venables said.

Oklahoma Sooners vs New Mexico Lobos in Week 3 college football, see top photos

Venables also said Stone's pain at the moment is a 2 out of 10.

The 6-foot-3, 315-pound star tackle is one of the best defensive linemen in college football with first-round NFL Draft talent. After a slow start to the season, Stone recorded a career-high eight tackles in the Sooners ' win over New Mexico .

The Del City native also registered two tackles for loss and a half sack against the Lobos.

If Stone misses time, OU will likely heavily rely on reserves like Nigel Smith II, Bishop Thomas and Trent Wilson . Boise State transfer Braxton Fely and Arkansas transfer Danny Saili, who both just joined the team, could also see more action.

The Sooners' first SEC availability report will be released Wednesday ahead of their game against Georgia .

articles.title: How Cubs Clinch Playoff Berth This Week, and Why Wild Card Top Spot Matters
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs have done a quality job of putting themselves in a good position entering the final week of the MLB regular season. They technically haven’t...
articles.body:
The Chicago Cubs have done a quality job of putting themselves in a good position entering the final week of the MLB regular season.

They technically haven't clinched a playoff spot yet in the NL Wild Card standings, but they're very close — and even once they do that, there'll still be more to play for.

The Cubs are opening the final week of the regular season with a three-game series in Wrigley Field against the Miami Marlins .

They'll then travel to Fenway Park to take on the Boston Red Sox in a three-game weekend set that could be impacted by bad weather in the Northeast.

Chicago still has a few different permutations for how the standings can look when all is said and done, so it'll be up to the Cubs to take care of business as best they can.

The Chicago Cubs enter Tuesday night's action with a magic number of 1.

That's in relation to the Arizona Diamondbacks , who are currently on the outside looking in for the playoffs.

If the Cubs get one more win, or the Diamondbacks lose even once, then Chicago will have secured a playoff spot.

Arizona still has six more games, too, so the Cubs need just 1-of-12 results to go their way in the final week of the season to ensure they're at least in the playoffs.

Even if that happens right away, though, don't expect the Cubs to let up.

The best of the three NL Wild Card teams gets an edge in the Wild Card Series.

That's because they're officially the National League's 4-seed taking on the 5-seed, and with that comes home-field advantage.

The Cubs would much rather play at Wrigley Field if possible.

The other three teams that could still make the other Wild Card spots are the Philadelphia Phillies , San Diego Padres and the longshot Diamondbacks.

The Cubs hold the tiebreakers in all three of those potential matchups, and they enter Tuesday tied with the Padres and ahead of the other two teams. That means the Cubs control their own fate here. If they put up better records the rest of the way than those teams, then the Wild Card Series is heading to Wrigley Field.

The key note is this: The Wild Card Series doesn't change ballparks. All potential three games in the best-of-three are played in the home of the better seed. That's why the Cubs would love to be atop the Wild Card standings.
