articles.title: Buffalo Bills Top Draft Pick Handed Harsh Outlook After Week 2
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills' 2026 rookie class hasn't had much of a role this season as top pick T.J. Parker hasn't played much. The post Buffalo Bills Top Draft Pick...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills ' 2026 rookie class hasn't had much of a role this season.

Buffalo traded out of the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft and ended up selecting pass rusher T.J. Parker in the second round out of Clemson.

Although the Bills are 2-0, Buffalo's rookie class has struggled, and their top pick was handed a harsh outlook.

Buffalo Bills Rookie Handed Harsh Outlook

Buffalo's rookies haven't had much of a role through two weeks, which has been common over the last couple of years.

With the Bills having a Super Bowl-contending team, it's hard for a rookie to make an impact right away. Yet, the hope was that Parker would be part of the pass rush, but that hasn't been the case, and Bills analyst Ralph Ventre of SI gave him a harsh outlook.

"Parker has been on the field for 22 percent of the defense's snaps as part of the edge rusher rotation, and he hasn't made a case for that number to increase. The second-round pick has one assisted tackle and no quarterback hits through two games," Ventre wrote .

Parker is behind Greg Rousseau , Bradley Chubb , and Michael Hoecht , which is why he hasn't gotten many snaps.

However, the Bills will need more pass rushers to rotate to keep everyone fresh, so Buffalo will need Parker to make an impact. Yet, through two weeks, the Bills coaching staff doesn't seem to have much confidence in their top pick.

Parker did have plenty of success at Clemson, but struggled in his final college season. Last year, he recorded just 5 sacks, but the year prior, he had 11 sacks and 19.5 tackles for a loss .

Whether or not Parker will get more snaps as he gets more comfortable as a pro and in the Bills system is to be seen. But for now, the rookie pass rusher isn't much of a factor in Buffalo's defense.

Jim Leonhard Reveals Concern for Buffalo's D

Although the Bills are 2-0, Buffalo's defense has struggled.

The Bills have a new defense with Jim Leonhard as defensive coordinator. Through two games, he believes the way they are playing defense isn't sustainable.

"We're kind of a boom-or-bust defense, and that's not okay long-term," Leonhard said after the win over Lions. "That's not sustainable. … When things have gone well in a drive, I mean, I think we're pretty much either three and out or touchdown right now over two games. I don't know exactly what the numbers are, but that's not far off from the truth."

Leonhard, meanwhile, expects the Bills defense to be much better.

"We're not playing our best ball," Leonhard said. "The numbers say that. We're all pissed off, but at the same time we're 2-0 and we're identifying our issues and we're going to go jump on them."

Buffalo will host the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 3.

articles.title: Red Sox remove Chad Tracy's interim tag, sign manager to 3-year deal
articles.summary: The Boston Red Sox removed Chad Tracy's interim tag and named him permanent manager through 2029, the MLB franchise announced Tuesday.
articles.body:
Sept. 22 (UPI) -- The Boston Red Sox removed Chad Tracy's interim tag and named him permanent manager through 2029, the MLB franchise announced Tuesday.

The Red Sox also exercised their 2029 and 2030 contract options on chief baseball officer Craig Breslow , who joined the franchise in 2023. Tracy took over as interim manager April 26 when the Red Sox fired former skipper Alex Cora. His pact includes a club option for 2030.

"Craig and Chad are two exceptionally talented leaders who have earned these opportunities in very different ways," Red Sox president and CEO Sam Kennedy said in a news release. "Over the last three years, we have watched Craig bring clarity, discipline and conviction to the work of building our baseball operation.

"Chad was asked to step into a difficult situation with little notice, but the trust he immediately commanded at the major league level was earned through years of work across our organization.

"What this team has accomplished over the past several months has been historic. Results matter greatly in this business, but so do judgment, character and the ability to bring out the best in others. Craig and Chad have demonstrated all of those qualities, and they have earned our confidence in leading us forward."

Tracy, 41, led the Red Sox to a 74-55 record through the first 129 games of his MLB managerial career. The Red Sox (84-72), who owned the second-worst record (10-17) in the American League the day Tracy assumed his former role, went on to clinch a wild card playoff berth.

Breslow, 46, previously spent time with the Chicago Cubs . The Red Sox went 254-226 over his three seasons in Boston.

The Red Sox will host the Cleveland Guardians (81-75) at 6:45 p.m. EDT Tuesday in Boston. They will host the Cubs (87-69) in their final series of the regular season this weekend at Fenway Park.

articles.body:
Benjamin Sesko Injury Blow for Manchester United After Slovenia Withdrawal

Manchester United have another problem to manage, and this one matters. Benjamin Sesko has withdrawn from the Slovenia squad after suffering a fresh setback with the shin injury that has been troubling him since last season.

For club and country, the timing is poor. Slovenia have Nations League games against Scotland , North Macedonia and Switzerland coming up, while United head into the break with little momentum and more questions than answers.

The striker had looked to be moving in the right direction. He started against Sabah in the Champions League and featured in four straight matches, a sign that his recovery was finally settling down. That optimism did not last long.

After 65 minutes in the Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton , the issue flared again. He was then left out of the trip to Fulham , where Michael Carrick confirmed the problem had returned. "It was a pain in his shin," said the United manager. "We're not sure with him yet. He felt a bit of pain after the game. We're assessing him. He definitely wasn't ready for today."

Manchester United statement outlines next step

United have already confirmed the immediate plan. "Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan." That is standard wording, but the situation is clear enough. There is no appetite to rush him back.

The injury dates back to May, when a collision with Ibrahima Konate at Old Trafford sent him into the advertising hoardings. He did not play again that season, missed pre-season completely and has had his minutes managed ever since.

Sesko is expected to spend the next three weeks at Carrington working through rehabilitation, with Tottenham on October 10 the likely target. Whether he makes that date depends on the tests and on whether this latest pain is a minor bump or another serious delay.

At 23, with 45 caps and 16 goals for Slovenia, Sesko remains a major asset. Right now, availability is the issue. For Manchester United, that has become a familiar and costly theme.

articles.title: After bolting Minnesota, Koi Perich is already feeling the heat at Oregon
articles.summary: Minnesota's former star safety is under the spotlight in Oregon, and a rough start has fans begging Perich for more.
articles.body:
Koi Perich's offseason decision to transfer from his home-state Gophers program to Oregon left a bitter taste in the mouths of Minnesota fans. His first three games with the Ducks have now left Oregon fans wanting more from their big-money transfer-portal addition.

Perich was one of the best high school football prospects to come out of Minnesota in the modern era. He was considered a four-star recruit and the No. 70-ranked player in the country, according to the final 247Sports Composite in the Class of 2024. His decision to stay home and play for the Gophers was a huge recruiting win for P.J. Fleck and his staff.

Perich lived up to the hype as a true freshman in 2024. He was a consensus first-team All-Big Ten player, finishing with 46 total tackles and five interceptions. The hype peaked ahead of his sophomore season.

A failed two-way experiment and underwhelming special teams performance contributed to Perich taking a huge step back in 2025. His Pro Football Focus (PFF) defensive grade cratered from 88.9 in year one to 61.0 in year two. His 23 missed tackles stuck out like a sore thumb.

Despite a very underwhelming 2025, Perich entered the transfer portal, and he was considered an elite portal prospect. He chose to remain in the Big Ten and play for Oregon over notable offers from Miami (FL) and Texas Tech, among other elite programs.

"I just wanted to be on a contender and a great program. I think Oregon is both of those. There's a lot of great coaches, great players here. And with both of those in the equation, you're going to have a lot of success. Hopefully I can add to that," Perich told the local Eugene media in August .

Perich earned a starting role on the Ducks defense, and he leads the team with 16 total tackles through three weeks. But analyzing his performance requires more context. He has seemingly corrected the tackling issues he had last year, with zero missed tackles so far this fall, but his coverage has statistically floundered.

Perich has 92 coverage snaps so far this season, and he has graded at 58.0, according to PFF. He has allowed a 126.2 passer rating into his coverage. Oregon's defense struggled in its first two games against Boise State and Oklahoma State, before a blowout win last week against FCS Portland State.

An anonymous Big Ten coach was even quoted by The Athletic as saying that Perich "isn't the same caliber player" as Dillon Thieneman, the Ducks safety who was selected by the Bears in the first round of the 2026 NFL Draft, and that Perich is "really struggling."

After an underwhelming start to the season, criticism of Perich has grown online. Some people from the Ducks' fan base are questioning why they let safety Kingston Lopa follow former defensive coordinator Tosh Lupoi to Cal, and others are calling for five-star freshman Jett Washington to see a bigger role.

"I've seen enough from Koi Perich. Get my dawg Jett on the field. Kid has it man you can just tell," one Oregon fan wrote on X.

"Koi Perich has shown me absolutely nothing good so far this year," another Ducks fan mentioned.

Oregon began the season as the preseason No. 2 team in the country, but they've fallen all the way down to No. 20. They certainly have the talent to be a championship contender, as Perich thought, but they have a small margin of error in Big Ten play to prove it.

Perich will look to block out the noise this week as Oregon has a huge game on the road against No. 12 USC. A loss to the Trojans and a 2-2 start to the season would only make the criticism around Perich's transfer decision louder — not just here in Minnesota, but also in Eugene.

articles.title: Byron Young wishes Jaxson Dart 'healthy recovery' after knee injury
articles.summary: Byron Young was involved in the play where Jaxson Dart got hurt, and he shared some kind words for the QB after the game.
articles.body:
Following the Los Angeles Rams ' victory over the New York Giants on Monday night, Pro Bowl linebacker Byron Young took to social media and wished Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart a healthy recovery. Young was involved in the play that forced Dart out of the game , hitting him on a third-down play during the opening drive.

On a routine third-and-eight on New York's first drive of the game, Dart dropped back for a pass. Young and fellow outside linebacker Josaiah Stewart shot around the edge of the offensive tackles, and as they closed in on Dart, they collided with him in a way that led to a knee injury. Dart attempted to return but was not able to.

Despite the accidental nature of the injury, Young shared his well wishes for Dart on Instagram.

While Young did nothing wrong, his class-act nature is another reason he's a respected and beloved player within the franchise. Young had an excellent performance in the win, recording five total tackles, one sack, one tackle for loss, and three quarterback hits.

For Dart, he is believed to have suffered a sprained MCL. Depending on the severity of the sprain, he could miss anywhere from one to six weeks.

articles.title: Clemson football, Georgia make shocking decision to cancel future series
articles.summary: Clemson and Georgia football programs have greed to cancel their future home and home series.
articles.body:
One of Clemson football's most familiar non-conference opponents is disappearing from the schedule for the foreseeable future.

Clemson and Georgia have canceled four games that were set for 2029, 2030, 2032 and 2033, according to the Athens Banner-Herald. The change removes two future trips to Athens and two scheduled games at Memorial Stadium.

The Tigers were supposed to host Georgia in 2029 and 2033, while the Bulldogs were scheduled to host Clemson in 2030 and 2032.

The move comes as both programs deal with less flexibility in future scheduling. Clemson is moving forward with a nine-game ACC slate while continuing its annual rivalry with South Carolina. The Tigers also begin an extended series with Notre Dame in 2027 and still have Oklahoma on the schedule for 2035 and 2036.

Georgia is facing a similar situation with the SEC expanding its conference schedule while the Bulldogs continue playing Georgia Tech each season.

That makes another Clemson-Georgia series more difficult to fit.

The two programs have played 66 times, with Georgia holding a 44-18-4 advantage. Clemson and Georgia were once regular opponents, including a stretch in which they met 24 times between 1962 and 1987.

Their most competitive run came from 1977 through 1987. Clemson and Georgia went 5-5-1 during those 11 meetings, with nine games decided by seven points or fewer.

The rivalry has become much less frequent since then.

Georgia has won the last three meetings, most recently beating Clemson 34-3 in Atlanta to open the 2024 season. With the four future games now canceled, another meeting between the Tigers and Bulldogs is not currently scheduled.

articles.title: Which Polk County football team is now ranked No. 1 in its class?
articles.summary: Polk County also has two football teams ranked in the top 12 overall in the state regardless of classification.
articles.body:
Gallery: Here is Lake Wales football in action in 2026

LAKELAND — Guess who is the No. 1-ranked team in Class 4A by MaxPreps? That's right, it's Lake Wales.

After its close loss to DeLand, now ranked No. 3 in Class 6A, Lake Wales has won four in a row and has shot up the rankings. Plantation American Heritage, which had been No. 1, dropped to No. 2 in 4A after losing to Lakeland, and district rival Orlando Jones, which had been ranked higher to start the season, is No. 4. Lake City Columbia is No. 3.

If there is an advantage to the ranking, perhaps it gives the Highlanders more confidence when they play Jones, Lake Wales' nemesis in recent years, in 2 1/2 weeks.

Lake Wales coach Tavaris Johnson is downplaying the ranking as coaches are prone to do.

"We're just going to keep focusing on each week, the opponent at hand," he said. "I'm doing my best not to try to fast-forward to Jones right now. We'll get there when we get there. Right now Brandon is in front of us, and we just got to make sure again we continue to build and compete and execute and finish."

Lake Wales (4-1) has Brandon (1-3) this week then has an off week before traveling to play Jones on Oct. 8 in Orlando. With the state championship being the ultimate goal, a No. 1 ranking is meaningless with one exception. It would give Lake Wales the home field throughout the playoffs up until the state championship game.

Here is where it gets interesting, however. Lake Wales also has climbed in the overall state rankings, moving up five spots last week and is now No. 12 overall, No. 11 if you exclude IMG which doesn't participate in the FHSAA playoffs. That's three spots from moving into the top eight and a spot in the Open Division. Lakeland is currently No. 9 overall and No. 8 when IMG is eliminated.

Being in the top eight isn't something that Johnson has thought about.

"I have not to be honest with you," he said. "I don't pay attention to a lot of that because it's data. Numbers don't lie, right? But I don't know the formula. I don't know what goes into it and tells me, so MaxPreps isn't simply judging how talented a roster looks. I think it's just, it's a computer and so when you think about that, what is the ranking what it really telling you? It's telling you that we've earned, some recognition, right? We've earned some respect. But there's still no room to prove. We got a lot of things to prove."

Lake Wales plays Brandon Friday then has an open week to get healthy and work on improving its weaknesses.

On paper, the weaknesses aren't obvious. The Highlanders have been a nearly unstoppable on offense, averaging 458.8 yards. They have scored 35 points or more in all five games, averaging 42.

Defensively, Lake Wales' first team has allowed just one touchdown — Winter Haven scored a late TD vs. the backups — in four games since losing to DeLand, 35-34, with two shutouts.

Yet coaches see more than what is on paper.

"Our focus is to be early, be prepared, be disciplined, be physical," Johnson said. "We got to get better. It's just the fundamental things — Kingston (Loydd) reading the defense better and just taking what they're giving them, offensive line finishing blocks, being physical, getting movement, receivers getting separation. We didn't build this program to be 12, right? We didn't build this program to be No. 1 (ranked), but we built this program to be the best version of Lake Wells that we possibly can be. So now we just gotta earn the next one. That's it. It's week to week for us."

Since going to the rankings to fill out the playoff teams after the district winners, replacing district runners-up, the FHSAA used its own power rankings, which it adapted from the MaxPreps rankings, to rank teams. This year, the MaxPreps rankings with no changes to the algorithm are being used to fill out the top eight teams in each region after taking out the top eight teams overall in the state for the Open Division.

With its current ranking and the fact that it should be favored in at least four of the remains five games — let's call the Jones game a coin flip — Lake Wales is well-positioned for a playoff berth.

"The bottom line is we have every reason to feel proud and validate it, but we go to stay hungry like we haven't proved anything yet," Johnson said.

articles.title: Florida great Louis Oliver to serve as Mr. Two Bits for Ole Miss game
articles.summary: Florida football legend Louis Oliver will serve in the celebrity Mr. Two Bits role against Ole Miss in the Swamp in Week 4.
articles.body:
Florida football legend Louis Oliver will serve as celebrity Mr. Two Bits on Saturday when the Gators host the Ole Miss Rebels inside Ben Hill Griffin Stadium.

Oliver began his collegiate career as a walk-on defensive back at Florida in 1984 and went on to earn numerous accolades before embarking on a successful professional career. He was a first-team All-American, a two-time first-team All-Southeastern selection and a two-time Academic All-American while wearing the Orange and Blue.

The 6-foot-2, 225-pound free safety finished his UF tenure with 11 interceptions returned for a cumulative 173 yards over 43 games. His season high came in 1987, when he snagged five picks for a conference-high 96 total return yards.

That same year, the speedy Oliver teamed up with three other football players — cornerback Tony Jones, receiver Ed Frazier and receiver Stacey Simmons — and recorded the fastest time in the country and the fourth-best time in the world in the 4x200 meter indoor relay, according to the university's archives.

After his redshirt senior campaign, Oliver was selected in the first round of the 1989 NFL Draft with the 25th overall pick by the Miami Dolphins — the team he went on to spend his first five seasons with, and six of his total eight years in the NFL. He earned All-Pro recognition for his efforts with the 'Fins in 1992, when he started all 16 games and ran back a pick-six — one of five interceptions that year — for a league-high 103 yards.

Oliver played alongside some of the greatest Gators to ever set foot in the Swamp and will join Lomas Brown, John L. Williams and Emmitt Smith as the only players from the 1980s to return to campus as a ceremonial Mr. Two Bits. He will be the second to lead the traditional cheer this season after Ciatrick Fason served in the role for Florida's home opener against FAU.

"I'm super-excited to get in front of Gator Nation again," said Oliver. "We're going to need all the motivation and ammunition we can get for this Ole Miss team."

The last time Oliver attended a game at the Swamp was Oct. 29, 1988, for Senior Day against Auburn. The Gators lost that game, 16-0, representing the last time the program was shut out.

Florida holds the longest streak in all of college football without being held scoreless, which currently stands at 477 straight games.

PHOTOS: Top highlights from Florida football's 2025 battle vs Ole Miss

About Florida football's Mr. Two Bits tradition

The Mr. Two Bits tradition began with George Edmondson, who led the crowd with his "Two Bits" cheer starting in 1950 until he retired from the role in 2009. From then to 2013, mascot Albert the Alligator donned the dress that Edmondson had worn throughout the decades while leading the fans with the same cheer.

This season marks the 14th year of the celebrity Mr. Two Bits tradition, in which a famous alumnus or a notable student earns the designation and is charged with the task of energizing the crowd alongside the Gators mascot.

articles.title: Yankees Reveal When They Will Activate Jazz Chisholm Jr. From Injured List
articles.summary: The New York Yankees should get Jazz Chisholm Jr. back on Tuesday
articles.body:
Jazz Chisholm Jr. has not played since Sept. 8 with a thumb sprain, but the New York Yankees are getting him back on Tuesday.

According to MLB.com's Bryan Hoch , Aaron Boone said that the Yankees expect to activate Chisholm between games of Tuesday's doubleheader against the Tampa Bay Rays .

The Yankees have a very slim chance of winning the American League East, but one loss against the Rays will end those chances. Getting Chisholm back does help their chances, even if he has not had his best season. Overall, Chisholm has a .232/.312/.403 slash line with 19 home runs.

He may not be having a season like last year's, but he was hitting his stride before the injury. From Aug. 4 to the point when he got hurt Chisholm had a .295/.388/.443 slash line with three home runs, two doubles, a triple, 10 stolen bases and 10 RBIs. In that span, he was second on the team in walk rate, fourth in strikeout rate, second in batting average, third in OPS and first in hard-hit rate.

The Yankees have some decisions to make when Chisholm is activated. For starters, they must decide who gets optioned. They will also have to decide where he plays. Chisholm is going to play every day if he's healthy, but that creates a problem for Anthony Volpe .

Volpe has been a solid hitter since returning from Triple-A, and the Yankees need to find a way to keep him in the lineup right now. With Chisholm back, Volpe's spot at second base is in danger. Could the Yankees move Chisholm back to third base to make sure Volpe and Chisholm are in the lineup together while both are hot.

articles.title: Chicago Wolves donate $3M to charities across area
articles.summary: The Chicago Wolves said this is about supporting the organizations that show up for Chicagoans every day.
articles.body:
The Chicago Wolves are used to putting points on the board. But Tuesday, the number that matters is $3 million.

The team said this is about supporting the organizations that show up for Chicagoans every day.

The $3 million will be distributed among dozens of nonprofit organizations across the Chicago area, each working to meet different needs in the communities they serve.

Representatives from many of those organizations joined the Wolves for Tuesday's announcement.

The recipients help provide everything from food and emergency assistance to care and opportunities for people with disabilities.

Misericordia is among the organizations receiving money. It provides a home, care and services to more than 600 children and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

The Salvation Army will also receive a $100,000 gift to support its work with people and families in need.

Other beneficiaries include Lurie Children's Hospital, the Ronald McDonald House... the Chicago Police Memorial Foundation and Special Olympics.

The Wolves said the larger initiative is designed to help these organizations continue work that reaches people throughout Chicagoland.

"I think it's a privilege to be in a position that we get to give back," Courtney Mahoney, Chicago Wolves president of operations. "Each and every game we get to do something for the community, throughout the season. But to do something as grandiose as this and to truly know the impact and how it's going to affect these charities and how it's going to affect other's lives is unbelievable."

The Wolves said the donations are a way to give back to a community that has always supported the team.

articles.title: Oklahoma: Venables hands Dabo Swinney, Clemson a big L in 4-star recruiting battle
articles.summary: The Oklahoma football team continues to build an impressive roster of elite young talent for the future. This was highlighted by the recent commitment of fou...
articles.body:
The Oklahoma football team continues to build an impressive roster of elite young talent for the future. This was highlighted by the recent commitment of four-star tight end Connor Arant from Bixby, who chose Oklahoma over offers from powerhouse programs such as Alabama , Ohio State , and Tennessee . Arant joins four-star quarterback Trey Tagliaferri as the second commitment in the 2028 recruiting class.

This offensive addition set the stage for an even bigger triumph on the recruiting trail against a familiar ACC rival. A major announcement shared by Hayes Fawcett on X revealed that four-star linebacker Jay Schell has officially committed to Oklahoma, selecting the Sooners over Dabo Swinney and Clemson . He excitedly declared, "BOOMER SOONER, I'm home!!!"

Schell's significant defensive commitment has brought a wave of excitement just as Brent Venables' squad prepares for a tough upcoming matchup against Georgia. However, the team is also dealing with a serious health concern. According to On3's Nick Schulz, star defensive lineman David Stone suffered an undisclosed lower-body injury during practice before the September 26 game. His availability for the matchup remains uncertain as he undergoes further testing.

As Oklahoma looks to improve its execution after a narrow win over New Mexico in Week 3, securing top prospects like Arant and Schell ensures that the program's long-term future remains exceptionally bright, even as they anticipate a challenging SEC schedule ahead.

articles.title: Tigers Double-A Manager Named Eastern League’s Best
articles.summary: The Tigers' Double-A manager was named Eastern League Manager of the Year in his first season. #Tigers
articles.body:
Tony Cappuccilli was named the Eastern League Manager of the Year on Monday, capping his first season in charge of the Erie SeaWolves , the Detroit Tigers affiliate at Double-A.

Tony Cappuccilli Wins Eastern League Manager of the Year

The SeaWolves announced the award on their X account. It is the latest step in a fast climb through the Tigers system for Cappuccilli, who managed the High-A West Michigan Whitecaps in 2024 and 2025 before Detroit promoted him to Erie for this season.

His 2025 Whitecaps team went 92-39 in the regular season, then went 4-0 in the postseason to win the Midwest League title. Baseball America named that club its 2025 Minor League Team of the Year.

Cappuccilli did not slow down at the next level. Erie went 79-58 in the Eastern League and finished first in the Southwest Division, the franchise's fifth straight division title and its fifth straight trip to the Eastern League Finals.

After the announcement, Cappuccilli wrote on X , "Thanks to our incredible staff I get to work with every day and all the amazing players who have been with us this year! I appreciate you all more than you know."

SeaWolves Face Elimination Tuesday Night

Erie reached the playoffs by winning the second-half title in the Southwest Division at 41-22, then swept the Richmond Flying Squirrels in the first round, 18-6 and 5-3.

The championship series has been tougher. Reading took Game 1 at UPMC Park on Sunday, 1-0, on a ninth-inning sacrifice fly, and the SeaWolves now trail the Fightin Phils 1-0 in the best-of-three. Game 2 is Tuesday at 6:45 p.m. at FirstEnergy Stadium in Reading, with Game 3 on Wednesday if Erie forces it. Cappuccilli is chasing his second straight minor league title in the Tigers organization.

articles.title: Jets to sign Will Levis to their practice squad
articles.summary: Will Levis has been out of the NFL since being cut by the Titans in August, but that's set to change.
articles.body:
Will Levis has been out of the NFL since being cut by the Titans in August, but that's set to change.

According to multiple reports, Levis is going to sign to the Jets ' practice squad. Levis worked out for the team earlier this month.

Levis was a 2023 second-round pick in Tennessee and he started nine games during his rookie season. He won the starting job in 2024, but went 2-10 as a starter and missed time with a shoulder injury before being benched for the final two games of the year. The Titans drafted Cam Ward first overall in 2025 and Levis wound up missing the whole year after having shoulder surgery.

Levis threw for 3,899 yards, 21 touchdowns and 16 interceptions while completing 61 percent of his passes across his 21 starts.

Geno Smith is the Jets starter with rookie Cade Klubnik as his backup. Bailey Zappe is currently on their practice squad.

articles.title: Yankees vs Rays live updates, analysis of day-night doubleheader
articles.summary: Follow along here as the Yankees host the Tampa Bay Rays in a day-night doubleheader at Yankee Stadium.
articles.body:
NEW YORK – Entering this day-night doubleheader at Yankee Stadium, the math is pretty simple.

With one win, the Tampa Bay Rays are the AL East champs and the Yankees are officially a wild card entry, likely to host the Boston Red Sox in a best-of-three next week.

"(We'll) try to push it off as much as we can,'' said Yanks manager Aaron Boone. "We want to play well.''

Boone's club also needs to prepare for postseason, which includes getting some players back – though Aaron Judge (calf strain) won't be one of them.

The slugging captain and defending AL MVP isn't in the Yanks' first-round playoff plans, per Boone.

But second baseman Jazz Chisholm Jr. (thumb sprain) should be activated off the injured list to start in the nightcap.

Right-hander Clarke Schmidt (biceps cramp) underwent tests Monday that showed "nothing significant.''

He'll play catch Tuesday and it "looks like he's in a pretty good spot,'' said Boone, though Schmidt's status won't be fully known until after he throws.

Ryan Weathers (flexor strain) is due to throw a bullpen session between games and is in play for activation before the first playoff round.

It's Tampa Bay righty Nick Martinez vs. Yanks' lefty Carlos Rodon in the doubleheader opener.
